title_es: Principios de diseño y el Marco Well-Architected
title_en: Design Principles and the Well-Architected Framework
body_es: El Marco Well-Architected de AWS proporciona una metodología comprehensive para evaluar y mejorar arquitecturas en la nube, basada en experiencias de miles de clientes. Se fundamenta en seis pilares estratégicos: excelencia operativa, seguridad, confiabilidad, eficiencia de rendimiento, optimización de costos y sostenibilidad (añadido en 2021). La excelencia operativa enfatiza la automatización de procesos y el monitoreo continuo de sistemas para identificar y resolver problemas proactivamente. La seguridad se logra mediante principios de defensa en profundidad, control de acceso granular y encriptación en todos los niveles. La confiabilidad se construye con redundancia arquitectónica, recuperación automática ante fallos y pruebas regulares de recuperación ante desastres. La eficiencia de rendimiento optimiza el uso de recursos computacionales mediante selección adecuada de servicios y monitoreo continuo. La optimización de costos maximiza el valor de la inversión mediante análisis detallado de gastos y eliminación de recursos no utilizados. La sostenibilidad minimiza el impacto ambiental de las cargas de trabajo en la nube: elegir regiones con energía más limpia, maximizar la utilización de recursos y diseñar para reducir el consumo energético. Estos seis pilares trabajan conjuntamente para guiar a los arquitectos en la construcción de sistemas escalables, seguros, económicamente viables y ambientalmente responsables.
body_en: The AWS Well-Architected Framework provides a comprehensive methodology for evaluating and improving cloud architectures, based on experiences from thousands of customers. It is built on six strategic pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability (added in 2021). Operational excellence emphasizes automation of processes and continuous monitoring of systems to identify and resolve issues proactively. Security is achieved through defense-in-depth principles, granular access control, and encryption at all levels. Reliability is built with architectural redundancy, automatic failure recovery, and regular disaster recovery testing. Performance efficiency optimizes the utilization of computing resources through appropriate service selection and continuous monitoring. Cost optimization maximizes return on investment through detailed expense analysis and elimination of unused resources. Sustainability minimizes the environmental impact of cloud workloads: choosing regions with cleaner energy, maximizing resource utilization, and designing to reduce energy consumption. These six pillars work together to guide architects in building scalable, secure, economically viable, and environmentally responsible systems. Implementing the Well-Architected Framework requires establishing governance processes and accountability within the organization. Teams should regularly review their workloads using the AWS Well-Architected Tool, which provides a systematic process to measure against all six pillars. The framework encourages automation of common operational tasks, continuous monitoring of system behavior, and proactive remediation of issues before they impact customers. Organizations that adopt this framework typically see improved reliability, reduced security risks, lower operational costs, and faster deployment cycles. The framework evolves continuously based on customer experiences and AWS innovations, ensuring relevance to emerging use cases and technologies.

# Enable AWS CloudTrail for operational visibility
aws cloudtrail create-trail --name well-architected-trail   --s3-bucket-name my-trail-bucket   --is-multi-region-trail

# Enable CloudWatch monitoring
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name HighCPUUsage   --alarm-description "Alert when CPU exceeds 80%"   --metric-name CPUUtilization   --namespace AWS/EC2   --statistic Average   --period 300   --threshold 80   --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold
